sahneler.metin: Two hundred thousand miles from Earth, an oxygen tank exploded.
In seconds, Apollo 13 lost most of its power and oxygen.
So how did a tank that passed every test just explode?
Its heater switches were rated for 28 volts, not 65.
They welded shut, and wires inside cooked at a thousand degrees.
Weeks later, in space, damaged wiring sparked inside pure oxygen.
The crew survived using the lunar module as a lifeboat.
One mismatched voltage nearly cost three lives.

aciklama:
On April 13, 1970, an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13, 200,000 miles from Earth. Its heater switches had been rated for 28 volts while ground equipment supplied 65.

vaka.yanilgi: Nothing hit Apollo 13. The failure was built in on the ground weeks earlier, when a mismatch in voltage ratings silently damaged the tank.
vaka.tartisma: The switches passed their own tests; the mismatch lived between two teams' specs. Who should own a failure that belongs to no single part?
